docs.title: Upgrading from 3.1 to 3.2
docs.text: This document summarizes the major new features, algorithmic optimizations, and output file changes in DNBelab C Series™ HT Single-Cell Analysis Software (dnbc4tools) between versions 3.1 and 3.2. Use the version switcher in the header to view the archived 3.1 documentation.

docs.title: Major New Feature: C6 Multiplexed scRNA Analysis
docs.text:
Version 3.2 introduces native support for C6 Multiplexed scRNA Analysis, enabling pooled multiplexed sequencing and high-precision sample demultiplexing within a single library:

  • Automated Execution: Declare sample names and associated Sample Barcodes in the [samples] section of the multi run configuration. The software automatically detects and runs the C6 multiplexed pipeline without requiring manual chemistry flags.
  • Comprehensive Pooled and Per-Sample Expression Matrices:
    • Complete gene expression matrices are generated for both the pooled library (in the root output directory) and for each demultiplexed sample (under per_sample_outs/<sample>/), provided concurrently in MEX directory, standard H5, and H5AD formats;
    • Each sample delivers a dedicated interactive HTML QC and analysis report (per_sample_outs/<sample>/<sample>_scRNA_report.html).
  • Sample-Specific BAM Outputs:
    • By default, generates dedicated aligned BAM files for each individual sample (per_sample_outs/<sample>/<sample>_alignments.bam with index), facilitating sample-specific IGV visualization and variant detection;
    • Reads not uniquely assignable to any sample barcode are collected in unassigned_alignments.bam.
  • Independent Dual-UMI Correction: Independently corrects and deduplicates both UMI segments for C6 dual-UMI architectures, ensuring high demultiplexing and quantification accuracy.

docs.title: 1. Single-Cell RNA (scRNA)
docs.text:
• Optimized Intra-Cell Multi-Gene Duplicate UMI Resolution:
    • Version 3.1 already supported this filtering mechanism, but had boundary condition defects. Version 3.2 resolves these defects and optimizes conflict resolution: when a UMI within a cell maps to multiple genes, it is assigned to the dominant gene with strictly higher read counts; if read counts tie, the ambiguous molecule is completely removed to eliminate artificial multi-gene co-expression and improve quantification fidelity.
  • Bound Safeguards for Automatic Cell Calling:
    • Version 3.1 lacked explicit upper and lower bounds for automatic cell number prediction. Version 3.2 introduces automatic prediction bound constraints, effectively preventing abnormal over-calling or extreme under-calling in low-quality or high-ambient RNA samples.
  • Optimized Read 2 Cell Barcode Filtering:
    • Refines quality control and filtering for Read 2 cell barcodes, more effectively identifying and error-correcting barcodes to retain more valid reads.

docs.title: 2. Single-Cell ATAC (scATAC)
docs.text:
• Cutsite-Based Quantification for Peaks and Matrices:
    • What is a cutsite? In ATAC-seq, Tn5 transposase binds open chromatin and cleaves the DNA double helix while inserting sequencing adapters, introducing a characteristic 9-bp staggered cut. Cutsite mode counts the actual Tn5 insertion cleavage endpoints after 9-bp offset adjustment. Compared to counting whole spanned fragments, cutsite mode directly and sensitively reflects local chromatin accessibility events.
    • Metric Semantics: Peak calling and matrix counts default to cutsite quantification; key QC metrics—including FRIP (Fraction of Reads in Peaks), TSS enrichment fraction, and Cell Calling—remain strictly evaluated on deduplicated unique fragments.

docs.title: 3. Single-Cell V(D)J (scVDJ)
docs.text:
• Improved chain pairing and contig assembly algorithms enhance full-length clonotype recall.
  • Enhanced multi-threaded sampling determinism guarantees reproducible results across identical inputs.

docs.title: Output Directory & File Format Changes
docs.text: Change Item Version 3.1 Version 3.2 Migration Action C6 Delivery Model Pooled analysis only Independent per-sample delivery of reports, matrices, and dedicated BAMs, plus pooled matrices (MEX / H5 / H5AD) Inspect per-sample results in per_sample_outs/<sample>/; global matrices are in the root directory. C6 Summary Table Uncompressed CSV outs/rna/singlecell.csv.gz Support gzip decompression; valid cells can be extracted using is_cell_barcode. RNA Matrix Directories raw_matrix/filter_matrix/ raw_feature_bc_matrix/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/ Aligned with standard 10X directory naming; companion .h5 files added for faster loading. ATAC Matrix Directories raw_peak_matrix/filter_peak_matrix/ raw_peak_bc_matrix/filtered_peak_bc_matrix/ Standardized directory naming; companion .h5 files added. ATAC Text Matrix matrix.mtx.gz tab-separated matrix.mtx.gz single-space separated Update custom scripts to split on whitespace (line.split()) or use standard MatrixMarket readers. Batch Analysis Scripts Written to output directory Generated only in the current working directory Run scripts from the current directory; --outdir sets analysis output; existing scripts are not overwritten.

docs.title: Quick Start Guide
docs.text: This guide provides end-to-end operational walkthroughs for the DNBelab C Series™ single-cell analysis suite (dnbc4tools), covering system prerequisites, reference genome indexing, single-modality pipelines, integrated multi-omics orchestration, C6 multiplexed single-cell RNA analysis, and batch analysis script generation.

docs.title: Choose a Workflow
docs.text:
Select the appropriate command entry point according to your experimental design and library preparation:

Workflow Command Entry Point Scope & Description Single-Cell RNA Analysis dnbc4tools rna run Single-sample gene expression quantification, EmptyDrops cell calling, and clustering Single-Cell ATAC Analysis dnbc4tools atac run Single-sample chromatin accessibility analysis, peak calling, and QC Single-Cell V(D)J Analysis dnbc4tools vdj run De novo TCR / BCR immune repertoire assembly, annotation, and clonotyping Integrated Multi-Omics dnbc4tools multi run --csv multi.csv Unified orchestration and cross-modality reporting for RNA + ATAC + VDJ C6 Multiplexed RNA dnbc4tools multi run --csv sample.config.csv Sample Barcode pooled RNA-seq de-multiplexing and per-sample dedicated delivery Batch Script Generation dnbc4tools <rna/atac> multi Batch-generate standalone analysis scripts for queued HPC scheduling

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before you begin:

  • Verify software installation and CLI availability. See the Installation Guide.
  • Replace $dnbc4tools in all example commands with your actual executable path (e.g., /opt/software/dnbc4tools3.2/dnbc4tools).
  • The backslash \ is used solely for multi-line layout in documentation and can be executed as a single continuous command line in your shell.

docs.title: --fastqs Directory Auto-Detection Rules
docs.text:
When using directory-based input via --fastqs <dir>, the pipeline automatically scans the folder and pairs paired-end reads matching the following patterns:

Read End Match Pattern Example Filenames Read 1 (R1) Contains _R1_, _R1, _1, or _read1 sample_R1.fastq.gz, sample_1.fq.gz, sample_R1_001.fastq.gz Read 2 (R2) Contains _R2_, _R2, _2, or _read2 sample_R2.fastq.gz, sample_2.fq.gz, sample_R2_001.fastq.gz
  • Supported Extensions: .fastq.gz, .fq.gz, .fastq, .fq
  • Explicit File Arguments Bypass Naming Restrictions: If files are provided via explicit flags (e.g., --fastq1/--fastq2 or RNA --cDNAfastq1/2, --oligofastq1/2), file names do not need to follow these patterns, but the list ordering between paired reads must match strictly.

docs.title: Single-Cell RNA Analysis
docs.text: Designed for standard single-sample 3′ or 5′ single-cell transcriptomic profiling and clustering.

docs.title: Step 1: Build Reference Genome
docs.text:
Using Human, Mouse, and Human-Mouse dual-species as common references:

Human (GRCh38) 

# 1. Download GENCODE annotation and genomic FASTA
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_human/release_32/GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_human/release_32/gencode.v32.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 2. Decompress files
gzip -d GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
gzip -d gencode.v32.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 3. Filter GTF and generate STAR genome index
$dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --ingtf gencode.v32.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf --output genes.filtered.gtf
$dnbc4tools rna mkref --ingtf genes.filtered.gtf --fasta GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa --threads 10 --species Homo_sapiens

Mouse (Mus musculus, GRCm38) 

# 1. Download annotation and FASTA
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_mouse/release_M23/GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_mouse/release_M23/gencode.vM23.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 2. Decompress files
gzip -d GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
gzip -d gencode.vM23.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 3. Filter GTF and generate STAR genome index
$dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --ingtf gencode.vM23.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf --output genes.filtered.gtf
$dnbc4tools rna mkref --ingtf genes.filtered.gtf --fasta GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa --threads 10 --species Mus_musculus

Human-Mouse Mixed-Species Reference 

# Combine FASTA and GTF after preparing both species
$dnbc4tools rna mkref \
    --fasta GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa,GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa \
    --ingtf hg38/genes.filtered.gtf,mm10/genes.filtered.gtf \
    --species hg38,mm10 \
    --threads 10

docs.title: Step 2: Run RNA Pipeline
docs.text:
Organize your sequencing files under structured subdirectories containing cDNA/ and oligo/. The pipeline will automatically identify and pair FASTQ files:

/test/data/rna_fastqs/          # Root directory passed to --fastqs
├── cDNA/                       # Transcriptomic cDNA sequencing reads
│   ├── sample_cDNA_R1.fastq.gz
│   └── sample_cDNA_R2.fastq.gz
└── oligo/                      # Bead/barcode Oligo sequencing reads
    ├── sample_oligo_R1.fastq.gz
    └── sample_oligo_R2.fastq.gz

Method 1: Directory Input (Recommended)

$dnbc4tools rna run \
    --fastqs /test/data/rna_fastqs \
    --genomeDir /database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens \
    --name test_rna \
    --threads 30

Method 2: Explicit Individual FASTQ Inputs

When sequencing files are not grouped into cDNA/ and oligo/ subdirectories, or are distributed across separate storage paths, specify each input file explicitly using dedicated arguments (comma-separated lists supported):

$dnbc4tools rna run \
    --cDNAfastq1 /test/data/cDNA/sample_R1.fastq.gz \
    --cDNAfastq2 /test/data/cDNA/sample_R2.fastq.gz \
    --oligofastq1 /test/data/oligo/sample_oligo_R1.fastq.gz \
    --oligofastq2 /test/data/oligo/sample_oligo_R2.fastq.gz \
    --genomeDir /database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens \
    --name test_rna \
    --threads 30

docs.title: Single-Cell ATAC Analysis
docs.text: Designed for single-cell chromatin accessibility analysis, peak calling, and transcription factor motif enrichment.

docs.title: Step 1: Build ATAC Reference
docs.text:
Human (GRCh38) 

# 1. Download GENCODE annotation and genomic FASTA
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_human/release_32/GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_human/release_32/gencode.v32.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 2. Decompress files
gzip -d GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
gzip -d gencode.v32.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 3. Filter GTF and build Chromap reference index
$dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --ingtf gencode.v32.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf --output genes.filtered.gtf
$dnbc4tools atac mkref --fasta GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa --ingtf genes.filtered.gtf --species Homo_sapiens --prefix chr

Mouse (Mus musculus, GRCm38) 

# 1. Download annotation and FASTA
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_mouse/release_M23/GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_mouse/release_M23/gencode.vM23.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 2. Decompress files
gzip -d GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
gzip -d gencode.vM23.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 3. Filter GTF and build Chromap reference index
$dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --ingtf gencode.vM23.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf --output genes.filtered.gtf
$dnbc4tools atac mkref --fasta GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa --ingtf genes.filtered.gtf --species Mus_musculus --prefix chr

Human-Mouse Mixed-Species Reference 

# Combine FASTA and filtered GTF after preparing both species (--prefix is not supported for mixed-species)
$dnbc4tools atac mkref \
    --fasta GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa,GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa \
    --ingtf hg38/genes.filtered.gtf,mm10/genes.filtered.gtf \
    --species hg38,mm10

docs.title: Step 2: Run ATAC Pipeline
docs.text:
Place sequencing files in a designated folder or provide paired-end files explicitly:

/test/data/atac_fastqs/          # Root directory passed to --fastqs
├── sample_R1.fastq.gz
└── sample_R2.fastq.gz

Method 1: Directory Input (Recommended)

$dnbc4tools atac run \
    --fastqs /test/data/atac_fastqs \
    --genomeDir /database/scATAC/Homo_sapiens \
    --name test_atac \
    --threads 10

Method 2: Explicit Individual FASTQ Inputs

$dnbc4tools atac run \
    --fastq1 /test/data/sample_R1.fastq.gz \
    --fastq2 /test/data/sample_R2.fastq.gz \
    --genomeDir /database/scATAC/Homo_sapiens \
    --name test_atac \
    --threads 10

docs.title: Single-Cell V(D)J Analysis
docs.text:
Designed for full-length TCR / BCR immune repertoire de novo assembly, annotation, and clonotyping.

Prerequisite: VDJ analysis requires matched 5′ scRNA-seq data. You must first execute the RNA pipeline with the --end5 flag to generate the cell-to-bead translation table singlecell.csv.

docs.title: Step 1: Run 5′ RNA Pipeline
docs.text:
$dnbc4tools rna run \
    --fastqs /test/data/rna_5p_fastqs \
    --genomeDir /database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens \
    --name test_rna_5p \
    --threads 30 \
    --end5

docs.title: Step 2: Run V(D)J Pipeline
docs.text:
Organize your sequencing files under a designated directory or provide FASTQ files explicitly:

/test/data/vdj_fastqs/          # Root directory passed to --fastqs
├── sample_R1.fastq.gz
└── sample_R2.fastq.gz

Method 1: Directory Input (Recommended)

Human TCR Analysis 

$dnbc4tools vdj run \
    --fastqs /test/data/tcr_fastqs \
    --beadstrans ./test_rna_5p/outs/singlecell.csv \
    --ref human \
    --name test_human_tcr \
    --threads 20 \
    --chain TR

Human BCR Analysis 

$dnbc4tools vdj run \
    --fastqs /test/data/bcr_fastqs \
    --beadstrans ./test_rna_5p/outs/singlecell.csv \
    --ref human \
    --name test_human_bcr \
    --threads 20 \
    --chain IG

Method 2: Explicit Individual FASTQ Inputs

When files are located in separate storage paths, provide them via --fastq1 and --fastq2:

Human TCR Analysis (Explicit Files) 

$dnbc4tools vdj run \
    --fastq1 /test/data/tcr/sample_R1.fastq.gz \
    --fastq2 /test/data/tcr/sample_R2.fastq.gz \
    --beadstrans ./test_rna_5p/outs/singlecell.csv \
    --ref human \
    --name test_human_tcr \
    --threads 20 \
    --chain TR

Human BCR Analysis (Explicit Files) 

$dnbc4tools vdj run \
    --fastq1 /test/data/bcr/sample_R1.fastq.gz \
    --fastq2 /test/data/bcr/sample_R2.fastq.gz \
    --beadstrans ./test_rna_5p/outs/singlecell.csv \
    --ref human \
    --name test_human_bcr \
    --threads 20 \
    --chain IG

Click to expand: Mouse TCR and BCR Analysis Examples

Mouse TCR Analysis

$dnbc4tools vdj run \
    --fastqs /test/data/mouse_tcr_fastqs \
    --beadstrans ./test_mouse_rna_5p/outs/singlecell.csv \
    --ref mouse \
    --name test_mouse_tcr \
    --threads 20 \
    --chain TR

Mouse BCR Analysis

$dnbc4tools vdj run \
    --fastqs /test/data/mouse_bcr_fastqs \
    --beadstrans ./test_mouse_rna_5p/outs/singlecell.csv \
    --ref mouse \
    --name test_mouse_bcr \
    --threads 20 \
    --chain IG

docs.title: Integrated Multi-Omics Analysis
docs.text: Designed for experimental workflows profiling RNA, ATAC, and V(D)J simultaneously from the same biological sample, providing coordinated execution and a unified interactive report.

docs.title: Step 1: Prepare Multi-Omics Configuration (multi_config.csv)
docs.text:
[libraries]
fastqs,feature_types
/test/data/rna,rna
/test/data/atac,atac
/test/data/vdj-t,vdj-t
/test/data/vdj-b,vdj-b

[rna]
genomeDir,/database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens
end5,true

[atac]
genomeDir,/database/scATAC/Homo_sapiens

[vdj-t]
ref,human

[vdj-b]
ref,human

docs.title: Step 2: Execute Multi-Omics Pipeline
docs.text:
$dnbc4tools multi run \
    --name test_multi \
    --csv ./multi_config.csv \
    --threads 20

Upon completion, the comprehensive interactive report test_multi_multi_report.html and individual omics subdirectories are delivered directly under ./test_multi/outs/.

docs.title: C6 Multiplexed Single-Cell RNA Analysis
docs.text: Designed for high-throughput experiments where multiple biological samples are pooled and tagged with Sample Barcodes before sequencing. The bioinformatics pipeline demultiplexes reads automatically and delivers isolated outputs for each individual sample.

docs.title: Step 1: Prepare C6 Configuration (sample.config.csv)
docs.text:
Create a configuration file containing [rna], [libraries], and [samples] sections:

[rna]
genomeDir,/database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens
no_bam,true

[libraries]
fastqs,feature_types
/test/data/c6_pooled_data,rna

[samples]
sample_id,probe_barcode_ids
Sample_01,BC01
Sample_02,BC02;BC03

Configuration Notes:

  • [samples] Section: Specifies each biological sample name and its assigned Sample Barcode tag(s). If multiple barcodes belong to a single sample, separate them with semicolons ; (e.g., BC02;BC03).
  • Sequencing Data Directory: /test/data/c6_pooled_data must contain the pooled cDNA/ and oligo/ subdirectories and FASTQ files.

docs.title: Step 2: Execute C6 Pipeline
docs.text:
$dnbc4tools multi run \
    --name test_c6 \
    --csv ./sample.config.csv \
    --threads 40

docs.title: Step 3: Core Deliverables
docs.text:
Upon completion, outputs are archived under ./test_c6/outs/:

  • Batch Summary Report: test_c6_multi_report.html, providing comparative cell yields, sequencing saturation, and throughput metrics across all demultiplexed samples;
  • Global Combined Feature-Barcode Matrix: rna/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/ (delivered in MEX, H5, and H5AD formats);
  • Global Single-Cell Bead Metrics: rna/singlecell.csv.gz (streamed gzip compression with is_cell_barcode cell annotations);
  • Per-Sample Isolated Outputs: rna/per_sample_outs/<sample>/, containing independent expression matrices, dedicated alignment BAM files (<sample>_alignments.bam), and interactive HTML reports.

docs.title: Batch Script Generation
docs.text: Designed for scaling up analysis across dozens of independent single-cell samples. By providing a tab-separated sample list, dnbc4tools automatically generates standalone shell scripts for each sample, ready to run directly or queue through workload managers such as Slurm or SGE.

docs.title: Step 1: Prepare Sample Manifest
docs.text:
RNA Sample Manifest (rna_samples.tsv)

Tab-delimited with 3 columns: sample_id, cDNA_R1;cDNA_R2, oligo_R1;oligo_R2 (comma-separated for multi-lane files per read):

Sample1 sample1_cDNA_R1.fq.gz;sample1_cDNA_R2.fq.gz sample1_oligo_R1.fq.gz;sample1_oligo_R2.fq.gz
Sample2 sample2_cDNA_R1.fq.gz;sample2_cDNA_R2.fq.gz sample2_oligo_R1.fq.gz;sample2_oligo_R2.fq.gz

ATAC Sample Manifest (atac_samples.tsv)

Tab-delimited with 2 columns: sample_id, FASTQ_R1;FASTQ_R2 (comma-separated for multi-lane files per read):

Sample1 sample1_R1.fq.gz;sample1_R2.fq.gz
Sample2 sample2_R1.fq.gz;sample2_R2.fq.gz

docs.title: Step 2: Generate Analysis Scripts
docs.text:
# Batch generate RNA execution scripts
$dnbc4tools rna multi \
    --list ./rna_samples.tsv \
    --genomeDir /database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens \
    --threads 20

# Batch generate ATAC execution scripts
$dnbc4tools atac multi \
    --list ./atac_samples.tsv \
    --genomeDir /database/scATAC/Homo_sapiens \
    --threads 20

Execution Behavior: The multi command generates standalone .sh scripts (e.g., run_Sample1.sh) in the current working directory without automatically starting computational workloads. Execute generated scripts on demand (e.g., sh run_Sample1.sh) or submit them to your HPC cluster queue.

After completing the quick start walkthroughs, consult detailed documentation for advanced options:

  • Explore underlying pipeline workflows: Pipeline Overview
  • Learn comprehensive parameters and CLI options: Parameters Overview
  • Understand structured deliverable files: Output Deliverables Overview

docs.title: Release Notes
docs.text:
Release history of DNBelab C Series™ HT Single-Cell Analysis Software

Latest Release • Published Releases • Version Guide

docs.title: Latest Release
docs.text:
dnbc4tools 3.2 — source documentation (unreleased), updated October 23, 2026.

The formal release date, installation package and checksums await confirmation. The latest release documented before this update was 3.1 (May 15, 2026).

docs.title: 3.2 changes
docs.text:
• C6 Sample Barcode multiplexing support: sample assignment, per-sample calling/analysis, independent RNA reports and batch comparisons.
  • Canonical RNA/ATAC matrix paths with H5 exports; complete compressed C6 singlecell.csv.gz, including background and zero-UMI rows.
  • Explicit ATAC defaults: ordmag calling, cutsite peak signal/matrix, all merged fragments for peak input, optional final fragment/TSS thresholds and low-targeting filtering.
  • Validated STAR arguments, GTF conflict policy, consistent parameter types and dark-cycle rules.
  • Preflight diagnostics, structured errors, run locks/checkpoints, safer batch script publication and automatic BAM resource scheduling.
  • Rust summary/matrix/BAM paths reduce redundant processing and use bounded intermediate handling. Actual speed and memory depend on the task; no universal speedup is claimed.

See the Upgrade Guide for behavior changes and matched Python/native requirements. Use the header menu to open the frozen 3.1 manual.

docs.title: Multi-omics Analysis
docs.text: • New Multi-omics Mode: Added support for single-sample multi-omics analysis. Now supports RNA + VDJ combined analysis or individual omics analysis.

docs.title: RNA Analysis Enhancements
docs.text: • Consistent Cell Analysis: Added new parameter --consistent_cells to enable analysis using existing merged results and cell assignments for consistent downstream processing.

docs.title: RNA Analysis Bug Fixes
docs.text:
• Fraction Reads in Cells: Fixed calculation error in "fraction reads in cells" metric.
  • Species Database: Fixed bug that occurs when single species contains underscore "_" in dual-species database.

docs.title: Performance Optimization
docs.text: • Speed Improvement: Optimized processing speed for bam2fastq and fqsubC4 tools.

docs.title: Configuration & CLI Fixes
docs.text: • CLI Consistency: Standardized help text and metavar formatting across modules, including multi-sample commands.

docs.title: Previous Version Notes (3.0 and Earlier)
docs.text:
The previous release records are listed below in reverse chronological order:

3.0 (Dec 18, 2025) 2.1.3 (October 9, 2024) 2.1.2 (April 24, 2024) 2.1.1 (September 21, 2023) 2.1.0 (July 28, 2023) 2.0.7 (November 4, 2022) 2.0.6 (September 19, 2022) 2.0.5 (August 19, 2022) 2.0.0 (June 20, 2022)

docs.title: RNA-Seq Enhancements
docs.text:
• Alignment & Annotation: Refined prioritization of exonic loci to improve quantification accuracy and resolve multi-gene mapping ambiguities.
  • Barcode Processing: Implemented error correction logic for cell barcodes containing ambiguous 'N' bases.
  • Dual-Species Support: Added robust support for building and analyzing mixed-species reference genomes.
  • Output Improvements: Enriched BAM files with cell tags (CC/CB), updated feature matrices to include gene ID, gene name, and library type.
  • Parameter Updates: Introduced automatic estimation for expectcells and added a new minumi threshold parameter.

docs.title: ATAC-Seq Enhancements
docs.text:
• QC & Reporting: Expanded QC metrics to include barcode/read Q30 statistics and insert size distributions derived from deduplicated fragments.
  • Technical Updates: Upgraded alignment engine to chromap v0.3.3, enhanced barcode correction algorithms, and enriched BAM outputs.

docs.title: VDJ Enhancements
docs.text:
• Assembly & Annotation: Advanced per-cell assembly algorithms to maximize full-length contig recovery with stricter filtering criteria.

docs.title: Before running
docs.text:
Confirm dnbc4tools --version is 3.2, validate paired FASTQs, reference and chemistry, and deploy native tools matched to Python. Logs are under <outdir>/<name>/logs/. RNA, ATAC and VDJ write compact startup information to preflight.json. Existing processing/output trees are recorded there; choose a new sample name for a fresh analysis.

rna multi / atac multi only generate .sh files in the working directory and do not initialize analysis logs. multi run executes analysis with logs. Batch lists use TAB-separated columns, ; between R1/R2 and , between same-end lane files. Execute scripts only after generation succeeds. Malformed lists, duplicate samples, colliding script names and existing scripts fail explicitly. Move old scripts before regenerating them.

docs.title: Error messages
docs.text:
Error ID identifies one error occurrence; Error code identifies a broad category. Retain terminal output, command, configuration CSV and logs/errors.jsonl.

Error code First checks CLI-CONFIG Option names/types, required values and configuration sections INPUT FASTQ/barcode/matrix paths, permissions, pairing and completeness REFERENCE FASTA, GTF, STAR/Chromap indexes and reference configuration TOOL Stage log, external command, matched native/Python interfaces OUTPUT Output path, free space, permissions and artifact integrity INTERRUPTED Interruption cause and recoverable stages INTERNAL Retain Error ID, traceback and structured logs for investigation

docs.title: Existing artifact checks (advanced)
docs.text:
This internal diagnostic is omitted from normal top-level help but can be called directly:

dnbc4tools validate-artifacts --sample-dir /path/to/sample --level shallow
dnbc4tools validate-artifacts --sample-dir /path/to/sample --level deep   --json /path/to/artifact-validation.json

shallow performs lightweight checks; deep scans full file contents. An empty directory can report success after checking zero files, which does not prove analysis completeness. This is not real-data acceptance testing.

docs.title: Interruption, recovery and empty results
docs.text:
A run lock prevents simultaneous analysis in the same directory. Check the original job before handling a lock conflict; forced unlocking is not a normal retry procedure. Advanced --resume reuses checkpoints only when input, configuration, tool identity and output validation permit it. File existence alone does not prove completion. Recovery switches --keep-empty and --force-unlock are recorded in run state.

Zero cells, sample failure and analysis not run are distinct states. C6 records failures and continues other samples by default; review sample_failure_policy and per-sample status. Regenerating HTML cannot restore missing matrices or H5AD files. See the Upgrade Guide for BAM and output-name changes.

docs.title: C6 Multiplexed Analysis Outputs
docs.text: The output directory structure for C6 multiplexed single-cell RNA analysis is organized into two primary tiers: root combined deliverables for batch-wide quality comparison, and per-sample dedicated analysis folders for independent downstream single-cell exploration.

docs.title: Output Directory Structure
docs.text:
Upon completion, results are archived under <outdir>/<name>/outs/:

<outdir>/<name>/outs/
├── <name>_multi_report.html              # Batch multiplexed summary report
└── rna/
    ├── raw_feature_bc_matrix/            # Combined unfiltered expression matrix (MEX)
    ├── raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5          # Combined unfiltered expression matrix (H5)
    ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix/       # Combined filtered cell matrix (MEX)
    ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5     # Combined filtered cell matrix (H5)
    ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad   # Combined filtered cell matrix (H5AD, raw counts)
    ├── singlecell.csv.gz                 # Compressed droplet summary (including background)
    ├── metrics_summary.xls               # Experiment-wide summary metrics (TSV)
    ├── oligo.records.bam                 # Shared oligo alignment records (if BAM is enabled)
    ├── unassigned_alignments.bam         # Alignments from unassigned reads (if BAM is enabled)
    ├── multi_sample/                     # Probe assignment and multiplexing metrics
    │   ├── per_sample_metrics.csv        # Cross-sample comparison metrics table
    │   ├── sample_metrics_summary.xls    # Detailed sample-level QC metrics
    │   ├── barcode_assignment_metrics.json # Probe de-multiplexing statistics
    │   └── high_occupancy_metrics.json   # High-occupancy droplet filtering metrics
    └── per_sample_outs/<sample>/         # [Per-sample independent deliverable directory]
        ├── raw_feature_bc_matrix/        # Sample-specific unfiltered matrix
        ├── raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5
        ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix/   # Sample-specific filtered matrix (MEX)
        ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 # Sample-specific filtered matrix (H5)
        ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad # Sample-specific filtered matrix (H5AD)
        ├── <sample>_scRNA_report.html    # Dedicated interactive sample HTML report
        ├── metrics_summary.xls           # Sample-specific metrics table
        ├── <sample>_alignments.bam       # Dedicated sample BAM (with .bai / .csi)
        └── analysis/                     # Dedicated clustering and marker gene analysis
            ├── clustering/               # Graph-based clustering results
            ├── diffexp/                  # Differential expression & marker gene tables
            ├── pca/                      # PCA dimensional reduction coordinates
            ├── tsne/                     # t-SNE visualization coordinates
            └── umap/                     # UMAP visualization coordinates

docs.title: 1. Batch Multiplexed Summary Report (<name>_multi_report.html)
docs.text:
• Purpose: Overview of the multiplexed run across all pooled samples.
  • Key Sections:
  • Batch Overview: Summary of cell counts, assigned reads fraction, and sequencing depth across samples;
  • Library QC: Shared cDNA and Oligo base quality (Q30), adapter trimming, and valid barcode rates;
  • Sample Comparison: Side-by-side interactive bar and scatter plots comparing median genes per cell, median UMI counts, and mitochondrial percentages.

docs.title: 2. Root Combined Matrices (filtered_feature_bc_matrix.*)
docs.text:
• Purpose: Unified count matrices pooling called cells across all biological samples in MEX, H5, and H5AD formats.
  • Design Note: Preserves raw gene expression counts without cross-sample joint clustering or UMAP projections. This prevents uncorrected batch effects from generating spurious clusters, enabling researchers to perform rigorous integration using tools such as Harmony or Scanorama downstream.

docs.title: 3. Compressed Droplet Summary (singlecell.csv.gz)
docs.text:
Stream-compressed gzip file containing comprehensive metrics for every bead/droplet, including background:

Column Description cell Aggregated cell identifier reads Total transcriptomic reads mapped to the bead/droplet gene Number of distinct genes detected umi Total unique transcript molecules (UMIs) detected is_cell_barcode True cell flag (1 or True indicates a called cell; 0 or False indicates background) barcode Original cellular barcode with Sample Barcode suffix

Downstream Analysis Tip: When analyzing this file in Python or R, always filter rows by is_cell_barcode == 1 to isolate true biological cells.

docs.title: 4. Per-Sample Dedicated Subdirectories (per_sample_outs/<sample>/)
docs.text:
Each biological sample receives a complete, independent deliverable matching standard single-cell runs:

  • Interactive HTML Report (<sample>_scRNA_report.html): Sample-specific barcode rank plot, clustering UMAP/t-SNE, and marker gene heatmaps;
  • Independent Matrices: MEX, H5, and AnnData (H5AD) formatted count matrices containing sample-level clusters;
  • Sample-Specific BAM (<sample>_alignments.bam): Contains only reads assigned to this sample, ready for direct visualization in IGV.

docs.title: Metric Denominators & Interpretation
docs.text: Metric Scope & Calculation Assigned Reads Read pairs assigned to this specific sample based on Sample Barcode matching (not total pooled raw reads) Mean Reads per Cell Assigned Reads / Cells within the sample (shows N/A if cell count is 0) Fraction Reads in Cells Confident transcriptomic reads in cells divided by all confident reads for valid barcodes in this sample Mapping Quality Evaluated against all reads assigned to the sample cDNA Valid Barcodes Reflects 100% when Assigned Reads > 0 (measures the assigned population) Library QC (Q30 / Valid UMI) Shared across the entire pooled sequencing run; labeled with cDNA QC scope in reports Sample Barcode Valid Rate Percentage of Oligo reads matching designed barcode whitelists based on observed statistics

docs.title: scATAC Analysis Output
docs.text: Single-Cell ATAC Sequencing Output File Guide

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
After single-cell ATAC sequencing analysis is complete, a standardized structure of files and subdirectories is generated in the specified output directory for chromatin accessibility analysis and epigenomic research.

Tip: All output files use standard formats compatible with mainstream single-cell epigenomic analysis tools (e.g., Signac, ArchR), adhering to internationally accepted data format standards.

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
.
├── alignment.fragments.sorted.tagged.bam       # QC-filtered alignment results (requires 'need_bam' parameter for analysis)
├── alignment.fragments.sorted.tagged.bam.bai   # Index file for the alignment results
├── filtered_peak_bc_matrix/                         # Directory for the filtered peak matrix in MEX format
│   ├── barcodes.tsv.gz                         # Barcode information for filtered cells
│   ├── matrix.mtx.gz                           # Peak signal data in sparse matrix format for filtered data
│   └── peaks.bed.gz                            # Peak position information for filtered data
├── fragments.tsv.gz                            # Contains all fragments aligned to the genome
├── fragments.tsv.gz.tbi                        # Index file for fragments, for fast random access
├── filtered.fragments.tsv.gz                   # QC-filtered ATAC fragment file, containing only fragments from filtered cells
├── filtered.fragments.tsv.gz.tbi               # Tabix index for the filtered fragments file, for fast querying of genomic intervals
├── metrics_summary.xls                         # Summary table of analysis quality metrics
├── raw_peak_bc_matrix/                            # Directory for the raw peak matrix in MEX format
│   ├── barcodes.tsv.gz                         # Raw cell barcode information
│   ├── matrix.mtx.gz                           # Raw peak signal data in sparse matrix format
│   └── peaks.bed.gz                            # Raw peak position information
├── raw_peak_bc_matrix.h5
├── filtered_peak_bc_matrix.h5
├── singlecell.csv                              # Summary table of cell information
└── *_scATAC_report.html                        # Analysis report in HTML format

Raw and filtered peak matrices also have H5 exports. Matrix counts default to cutsites; cell calling, FRIP and TSS fractions retain unique-fragment statistics. BAM requires --need_bam; indexes can be BAI or CSI.

docs.title: ATAC Fragment and Peak Files
docs.text: Core Content: ATAC-seq fragment information and peak identification results, containing complete chromatin accessibility data and cell barcode tags.

docs.title: fragments.tsv.gz
docs.text:
fragments.tsv.gz is a compressed TSV file containing ATAC-seq fragment information, which is one of the core data for downstream analysis. Its main features and contents are as follows:

  • Purpose:

    • Chromatin Accessibility Analysis: Precisely locate the genomic coordinates of each open chromatin region.
    • Data Visualization: Can be directly loaded as a BED file in genome browsers like IGV and UCSC for visualization.
    • Downstream Tool Input: Compatible with mainstream single-cell analysis tools such as ArchR and Signac.

  • Content & Format:

    • The file is in BED-like format, with each row representing a unique ATAC-seq fragment.

    • The file contains the 5 columns of information as shown in the table below:

      Field Name Description chrom The name of the reference genome chromosome, identifying the chromosomal location of the fragment. chromStart The adjusted start position of the fragment on the chromosome (0-based), corrected for the transposase cleavage site. chromEnd The adjusted end position of the fragment on the chromosome (exclusive), corrected for the transposase cleavage site. barcode The cell ID identifier, corresponding to the CB tag in the BAM file, used to assign the fragment to a specific cell. readSupport The total number of read pairs associated with this fragment (including unique and duplicate reads).

  • Coordinate Adjustment:

    • To accurately locate the transposase cleavage site, the fragment intervals in the file are adjusted: the start position is shifted 4bp forward from the leftmost alignment position, and the end position is shifted 5bp backward from the rightmost alignment position.

docs.title: fragments.tsv.gz.tbi
docs.text:
The Tabix index file for fragments.tsv.gz.

  • Core Purpose:
    • Fast Data Access: Allows for rapid, genome-interval-based querying of large fragments.tsv.gz files without reading the entire file.
    • Tool Performance Optimization: Used by tools like ArchR, Signac, and IGV to load and process data from specific regions.
  • Format:
    • A standard binary index file generated by the tabix tool.

docs.title: filtered.fragments.tsv.gz
docs.text:
This is the ATAC-seq fragment file after cell quality control and filtering. It is a subset of fragments.tsv.gz, containing only fragments from high-quality cells.

  • Core Purpose:
    • Core Downstream Analysis: This is the recommended input file for core downstream steps such as cell clustering and differential accessibility analysis.
    • Improved Signal-to-Noise Ratio: Using this file improves the accuracy and signal-to-noise ratio of the analysis results by removing low-quality cells and background noise.
  • Content & Format:
    • The file format is identical to fragments.tsv.gz (compressed BED-like TSV) and contains the same 5 columns.
    • It includes only fragments from barcodes identified as "real cells" by the cell filtering algorithm (e.g., based on TSS enrichment and number of fragments in peaks).

docs.title: filtered.fragments.tsv.gz.tbi
docs.text:
The Tabix index file for filtered.fragments.tsv.gz.

  • Core Purpose:
    • Downstream Analysis Support: Ensures that downstream tools (like ArchR, Signac) can quickly access data from specific genomic regions when using the filtered fragment file.
  • Format:
    • A standard binary index file generated by the tabix tool.

docs.title: alignment.fragments.sorted.tagged.bam
docs.text:
This is the ATAC-seq alignment result file containing all fragments that have a valid barcode and were successfully aligned.

  • Core Purpose:

    • In-depth Analysis & Visualization: Can be used in genome browsers like IGV for deep visualization to inspect alignments at specific loci.
    • Custom Analysis: Provides the raw input for advanced users who need to directly manipulate alignment-level data.

  • Content & Format:

    • Uses the international standard BAM (Binary Alignment Map) format.
    • The file is sorted by genomic coordinates and indexed (with a .bai file) for fast random access.
    • Each read is tagged with cell origin information via TAG fields.

  • Key TAG Field Descriptions:

    • Cell and molecular barcode information is stored in the following TAG fields:

      Tag Type Description CB Z Cell barcode identifier after error correction and cell merging. CC Z Error-corrected cell barcode sequence. CR Z Cell barcode sequence as reported by the sequencer.

docs.title: alignment.fragments.sorted.tagged.bam.bai
docs.text:
The index file for alignment.fragments.sorted.tagged.bam.

  • Core Purpose:
    • Fast Data Access: Allows tools like IGV and Samtools to quickly jump to and read alignment data from any genomic region without loading the entire BAM file.
    • Performance Guarantee: Essential for the performance of any tool that performs random access operations on the BAM file.
  • Format:
    • Standard BAI (BAM Index) format generated by the samtools index command.

docs.title: Peak Matrix Files
docs.text: Core Content: The single-cell peak signal count matrix, divided into raw and quality-controlled filtered data, using the standard sparse matrix format.

docs.title: Filtered Peak Matrix (filtered_peak_bc_matrix/)
docs.text:
Contains the peak count matrix after high-quality cell filtering, serving as the core data for downstream quantitative analysis.

  • Core Purpose:

    • Downstream Quantitative Analysis: The primary input for analyses such as cell clustering, differential accessibility analysis, and trajectory inference.
    • High-Quality Data: Contains only barcodes identified as real cells, ensuring the accuracy of the analysis results.

  • Content & Format:

    • Uses the standard Matrix Market Exchange (MEX) format, consisting of the following three compressed files: Filename Description barcodes.tsv.gz A list of cell IDs, identifying high-quality cells that passed QC. Each line contains one cell ID, corresponding to a column in the matrix. peaks.bed.gz A file with peak region coordinates in BED format. Contains chromosome, start, and end positions, corresponding to a row in the matrix. matrix.mtx.gz The peak region count matrix in Matrix Market format. Contains matrix dimensions and the row, column, and value for non-zero elements.

  • Format Advantages:

    • Space-Efficient: The sparse matrix format (.mtx) saves significant storage space by only storing non-zero elements.
    • Highly Compatible: The MEX format is a standard in the single-cell community, compatible with almost all mainstream analysis tools like Seurat, Signac, Scanpy, etc.

docs.title: Raw Peak Matrix (raw_peak_bc_matrix/)
docs.text:
Contains the raw peak count matrix for all detected cell barcodes (without filtering).

  • Core Purpose:

    • Quality Control Assessment: Can be used to evaluate the effectiveness of cell filtering or to perform manual filtering based on custom criteria.
    • Data Integrity: Preserves all original data, which can be used for deep mining or re-analysis if needed.

  • Content & Format:

    • Uses the standard Matrix Market Exchange (MEX) format, with the same file composition as the filtered_peak_bc_matrix/ directory.
    • Includes all detected barcodes, including high-quality cells, low-quality cells, and background droplets.

docs.title: Analysis Summary
docs.text: Core Content: A summary of experimental quality assessment and statistical metrics, providing complete data quality control information.

docs.title: metrics_summary.xls
docs.text:
An Excel-formatted summary table of key analysis metrics, providing a structured assessment of the overall experiment quality.

  • Core Purpose:

    • Quality Assessment: Quickly evaluate key metrics such as sequencing data quality, alignment efficiency, and cell identification results.
    • Results Overview: Provides a summary view of the analysis results without inspecting all files.

  • Content & Format:

    • Contains key metrics from three main categories: Metric Category Includes Basic Stats Basic sequencing metrics like total read pairs, valid barcode ratio, Q30 base quality, etc. Cell Calling Cell calling results like estimated number of cells, fraction of fragments in peaks, fraction of fragments in TSS, number of peaks detected, TSS enrichment, etc. Alignment Alignment statistics like genome alignment rate, mitochondrial DNA ratio, etc.

    • Includes built-in recommended quality control thresholds for user convenience: Recommended Quality Thresholds:

      • Valid Barcode Ratio: >70%
      • Q30 Base Quality: >75% (Barcode and UMI regions)
      • Genome Alignment Rate: >50%
      • TSS Enrichment Score (Human/Mouse): >4
      • Fraction of Fragments in Peaks: >15%
      • Fraction of Fragments in TSS: >10%
      • Percentage of Duplicate Reads: >10%

docs.title: singlecell.csv
docs.text:
singlecell.csv includes Cell,totalFrags,fragments,mt_region_fragments,chloroplast_region_fragments,TSS_region_fragments,blacklist_region_fragments,peaks_number,peak_region_fragments,peak_region_cutsites,is_cell_barcode,Cellbarcode. The peak-region fragment and cutsite columns represent distinct counts. A missing cutsite statistic from an older tool is not zero. A CSV-formatted table of cell-level quality control information, recording detailed statistics for each cell barcode.

  • Core Purpose:

    • Fine-grained QC: Allows users to perform more detailed cell filtering and analysis based on custom criteria.
    • Downstream Analysis Input: Can be used as cell metadata input for analysis tools like Signac and Scanpy.

  • Content & Format:

    • Each row represents one cell barcode.
    • Key columns include: number of fragments, number of peaks, number of fragments in TSS/peak regions, whether it is identified as a high-quality cell, bead merging information, etc.

docs.title: *_scATAC_report.html
docs.text:
An interactive HTML report for reviewing analysis results.

  • Core Purpose:

    • Results Visualization: Intuitively displays key analysis results such as QC metrics, cell clustering, and TSS enrichment in the form of interactive charts.
    • Results Interpretation: Provides the biological significance and technical explanation of various metrics to help users interpret the data deeply.
    • Easy Sharing: A single HTML file that is easy to circulate and share.

  • Content & Format:

    • Can be opened in any modern browser without an internet connection.
    • For a detailed interpretation of the report, please refer to the Web Report Interpretation section below.
    • Key content modules included are as follows: Report Feature Description Interactive Charts Interactive visualizations for QC metrics, cell clustering, peak analysis, etc. Statistical Summary A numerical summary and trend analysis of key performance indicators. Detailed Interpretation The biological significance and technical explanation of various metrics.

docs.title: File Format Description
docs.text: Technical Specification: A detailed description of the standard formats used for the output files.

docs.title: Matrix Market Format (.mtx.gz)
docs.text:
Market Exchange Format (MEX) is a standard format for storing sparse count matrices in single-cell analysis, known for its space efficiency and high compatibility.

  • Core Advantages:

    • Space-Efficient: The sparse matrix format only stores non-zero elements, which significantly saves storage space for single-cell data where over 95% of values are typically zero.
    • Highly Compatible: As an international standard, it can be directly read by almost all mainstream analysis tools, including Seurat, Scanpy, and Signac.

  • File Composition:

    • A complete MEX format dataset consists of the following three files: Filename Description matrix.mtx.gz A compressed sparse matrix file. The header contains matrix dimensions, and each subsequent line records the position (row/column index) and value of a non-zero element. barcodes.tsv.gz A compressed cell barcode file. Each line is a cell ID, and the line number corresponds to the matrix column. peaks.bed.gz A compressed feature (peak) file. Each line is a peak's coordinates in BED format, and the line number corresponds to the matrix row.

docs.title: Web Report Interpretation
docs.text:
Overview: The HTML web report provides visual summaries and metric explanations for single-cell ATAC sequencing results, including key performance indicators for experimental quality and downstream analysis.

The HTML web report is the main entry point for reviewing single-cell ATAC sequencing results. It covers cell calling, fragment quality, TSS enrichment, peak-related metrics, and clustering results, and helps users identify metrics that require further review.

Usage Notes: It is recommended to review the metrics in the order they are presented in the report.

Note: The following standards are for reference only. Actual quality assessment should consider factors such as sample type, cell state, and experimental goals. Since significant differences can exist between samples, we recommend interpreting the results in the context of your specific experimental background.

docs.title: Cell Metrics
docs.text:
Core Function: Cell identification, quality assessment, and chromatin accessibility statistics, providing key indicators for the overall effectiveness of the experiment.

Quality Control Standards:

Metric Name Recommended Acceptable Needs Improvement Median fragments per cell ≥ 10,000 2,000–10,000 < 2,000 Median fraction of fragments overlapping peaks ≥ 30% 15–30% < 15% Median fraction of fragments overlapping TSS ≥ 20% 10–20% < 10% Fraction fragments in cells ≥ 50% 20–50% < 20%

Detailed Metric Explanations:

Metric Name Detailed Explanation & Technical Requirements Estimated number of cells
  • Definition: The total number of valid cells identified from the sequencing data (as distinct from background noise or empty droplets).
  • Calculation Process: After merging barcodes from the same droplet, cells are filtered based on peak-overlapping fragment counts, TSS proportion, and related QC metrics.
  • Interpretation: Compare this value with expected cell loading, fragment-count distribution, and filtering results. If it is much lower than expected, review sample integrity, library quality, and sequencing depth.
Species
  • Definition: The species or reference genome version used for the analysis.
  • Use case: Confirms whether the reference genome used for analysis matches the sample species. This is a basic item for result review and troubleshooting.
Median fragments per cell
  • Definition: The median number of valid ATAC-seq fragments contained within a single cell.
  • Use case: Assesses the number of valid fragments available for open-chromatin analysis in each cell and reflects sequencing coverage.
  • Interpretation:
    • High-Quality Standard: ≥ 10,000
    • Recommended Minimum: ≥ 2,000
Mean raw read pairs per cell
  • Definition: The average number of raw sequencing read pairs assigned to each cell.
  • Calculation: `Total Raw Read Pairs / Estimated Number of Cells`
  • Interpretation: A value of ≥ 25,000 is recommended to ensure adequate chromatin coverage. Lower values may reduce the stability of peak calling, clustering, and differential accessibility analysis.
Fraction overlapping peaks
  • Definition: The proportion of a single cell's fragments that fall into identified open chromatin regions (Peaks).
  • Use case: Key metric for ATAC signal specificity. A higher proportion indicates that valid fragments are more concentrated in open chromatin regions and background noise is relatively lower.
  • Interpretation:
    • Needs attention: If < 15%, review nuclei quality, transposition efficiency, peak calling results, and sequencing depth.
Fraction overlapping TSS
  • Definition: The proportion of a single cell's fragments that fall within the ±2kb region of a Transcription Start Site (TSS).
  • Use case: Assesses promoter-proximal open-chromatin signal and ATAC-seq library specificity.
  • Interpretation:
    • Needs attention: If < 10%, interpret together with the TSS enrichment profile, fragment length distribution, and sample preparation workflow.
Fraction of fragments in cells
  • Definition: The proportion of all valid fragments that are successfully assigned to a high-quality cell ID.
  • Use case: Assesses how much valid fragment signal comes from high-quality cells and helps evaluate background fragments or empty-droplet effects.
  • Interpretation:
    • Needs attention: A low ratio may indicate high background fragments, abnormal filtering strictness, poor sample quality, or library construction issues.
Number of peaks
  • Definition: The total number of open chromatin regions (peaks) identified across the genome after aggregating the signal from all cells.
  • Use case: Assesses the number of detectable open chromatin regions and the coverage of regulatory elements in the sample.
  • Influencing factors: Affected by cell number, cell-type heterogeneity, sequencing depth, and peak calling parameters.
  • Typical Range: 50,000 – 150,000 peaks.

docs.title: Sequencing Metrics
docs.text:
Core Function: Basic quality assessment of sequencing data, including barcode identification rate, alignment quality, and sequencing accuracy.

Quality Control Standards:

Metric Category Recommended Acceptable Needs Improvement Valid barcodes ≥ 80% 70–80% < 70% Q30 bases in barcode > 85% 75–85% < 75% Q30 bases in read > 85% 75–85% < 75% Confidently mapped read pairs > 80% 50–80% < 50%

Detailed Metric Explanations:

Metric Name Detailed Explanation & Technical Requirements Total number of read pairs
  • Definition: The total number of raw sequencing read pairs allocated to the sample.
  • Use case: Represents the total data volume of the sequencing run and serves as the baseline for evaluating sequencing depth and downstream QC metrics.
Valid barcodes
  • Definition: The proportion of reads whose cell barcode sequence can be successfully matched to the predefined whitelist (with error correction).
  • Use case: Assesses whether cell barcode recognition is stable and whether fragments can be assigned to cells correctly.
  • Interpretation: A low proportion usually suggests barcode recognition issues, which may be related to barcode sequencing quality, contamination, or library preparation quality.
Confidently mapped read pairs
  • Definition: The proportion of all reads that successfully align to any location on the reference genome.
  • Interpretation:
    • Needs attention: If < 50%, review sample contamination, species selection, reference genome version, and sequencing quality.
Mitochondrial reads ratio
  • Definition: The proportion of all aligned reads that map to the mitochondrial genome.
  • Use case: Assesses mitochondrial-derived fragment proportion and helps evaluate nuclei preparation and sample integrity.
  • Interpretation: An excessively high ratio (e.g., > 10%) often suggests cell death, excessive lysis, or elevated mitochondrial DNA capture.
Nucleosome-free regions
  • Definition: The proportion of fragments originating from open chromatin regions (that is, nucleosome-free regions).
  • Use case: Assesses the proportion of fragments from open chromatin and reflects valid ATAC-seq signal strength.
  • Interpretation: A high proportion (e.g., > 40%) generally indicates strong chromatin accessibility signal and efficient transposition.
Mono-nucleosome regions
  • Definition: The proportion of fragment regions containing a single nucleosome.
  • Use case: Assesses mono-nucleosome fragment proportion and, together with nucleosome-free regions, helps evaluate chromatin structure integrity.
Q30 bases in barcode
  • Definition: The proportion of bases with a sequencing quality score of Q30 or higher in the cell barcode sequence.
Q30 bases in read
  • Definition: The proportion of bases with a sequencing quality score of Q30 or higher in the sequencing read.

docs.title: Visualization Chart 1
docs.text: Core Function: Multi-dimensional visualization for cell quality control, fragment analysis, and chromatin accessibility assessment.

docs.title: Barcode Rank Plot
docs.text:
Chart Function: This plot ranks all cell barcodes by fragment count to distinguish high-quality true cells from background noise.

How to Interpret:

  • Axes:
    • X-axis (Barcode Rank): All barcodes ranked in descending order by fragment count. Left = high-fragment barcodes; right = low-fragment barcodes.
    • Y-axis (Fragment Counts): Total peak-overlapping fragment counts per barcode (log scale).
  • Key Feature (Knee Point):
    • The curve usually has a clear "knee point".
    • The blue region to the left of the knee indicates barcodes identified as high-quality real cells.
    • The gray region to the right indicates background noise.
  • Interactivity:
    • Hover to inspect barcode rank and fragment count details.
    • Blue color intensity reflects the local density of real cells.

docs.title: Droplet Beads Distribution
docs.text:
Chart Function: Shows the distribution of captured cell barcodes (beads) within droplets identified as real cells.

How to Interpret:

  • Theoretical distribution: Bead count per droplet is expected to approximately follow a Poisson distribution, reflecting random capture in microfluidics.
  • Practical factors: The observed distribution is affected by sequencing saturation, droplet size uniformity, and cell concentration.

docs.title: Cell Data Distribution
docs.text:
Chart Function: Three violin plots show the distributions of key QC metrics in high-quality cells: Fragments, TSS Proportion, and Peak Proportion.

How to Interpret:

  • Violin plot basics:
    • Plot width indicates cell density at that value. Wider sections represent more cells.
    • The internal boxplot summarizes median and quartiles.
  • Metric interpretation:
    • Fragments: Distribution of total fragments per cell. Better libraries usually have a higher central density.
    • TSS Proportion: Distribution of fragment fractions around TSS. A higher center indicates stronger transcription-associated accessibility.
    • Peak Proportion: Distribution of fragment fractions in called peaks. A higher center indicates better signal-to-noise.

docs.title: Fragment Length Distribution
docs.text:
Chart Function: Shows the insert length distribution of deduplicated ATAC-seq fragments, a key plot for assessing sample quality and chromatin structure integrity.

How to Interpret:

  • Periodic peaks:
    • < ~100 bp: First peak, corresponding to nucleosome-free regions (NFRs), that is, open chromatin.
    • ~200 bp: Second peak, corresponding to mono-nucleosome fragments.
    • ~400 bp, ~600 bp: Subsequent peaks corresponding to di-nucleosome and tri-nucleosome fragments.
  • Quality assessment:
    • High-quality sample: Clear ~200 bp periodic peaks with a prominent NFR peak, indicating intact nuclei and clear chromatin structure.
    • Low-quality sample: Flat curve without periodicity, often indicating over-lysis or disrupted chromatin architecture.

docs.title: Percent duplicates
docs.text:
• Definition: The proportion of fragments identified as PCR duplicates.
  • Use case: Used to assess library complexity and sequencing saturation, and to determine whether additional sequencing is likely to be useful.
  • Quality interpretation:
  • High duplication (e.g., >20-30%) usually indicates sequencing has approached saturation and additional sequencing may have limited benefit.
  • Very low duplication (e.g., <10%) may suggest insufficient depth; deeper sequencing may recover more unique fragments.

docs.title: Jaccard threshold
docs.text:
• Definition: Similarity cutoff used to determine whether two beads came from the same droplet/cell.
  • Use case: In C4 ATAC, one droplet may contain multiple beads; the software uses bead-level fragment overlap (Jaccard index) to decide whether beads should be merged.
  • Algorithm: Automatically determined by Otsu's method. To ensure stability, if the computed threshold is < 0.02, it is set to 0.02.

docs.title: Visualization Chart 2
docs.text: Core Function: Advanced visualizations for cell clustering, TSS enrichment patterns, saturation assessment, and bead similarity.

docs.title: Cluster Analysis
docs.text:
Chart Function: Cells with similar chromatin accessibility patterns are grouped in 2D space using UMAP + Louvain clustering to identify potential cell subpopulations.

How to Interpret:

  1. Left plot (cell clusters)
    • Each point is one cell.
    • Different colors indicate different clusters, potentially representing distinct cell types or states.
    • Nearby points have more similar accessibility profiles.
  2. Right plot (fragment count overlay)
    • Uses the same UMAP layout with a color gradient for per-cell fragment count.
    • Darker colors indicate higher fragment counts and usually better data quality.

docs.title: TSS Enrichment Profile
docs.text:
Chart Function: Shows fragment insertion enrichment around transcription start sites (TSS), a core indicator of ATAC-seq signal specificity and quality.

How to Interpret:

  1. Axes
    • X-axis: Position relative to TSS (0 = TSS).
    • Y-axis: Normalized signal intensity (insertion frequency).
  2. Key pattern
    • High-quality data usually shows a clear enrichment peak at TSS center (0).
    • Signal should drop quickly away from the center.
  3. Quality assessment
    • TSS Enrichment Score quantifies this pattern; higher scores (e.g., >4-6) indicate better signal-to-noise.
    • Flat curves without a clear enrichment peak may suggest poor sample quality or library preparation issues.

docs.title: Single Cell Targeting Plot
docs.text:
Chart Function: A scatter plot of two key QC metrics per cell, used to evaluate cell-calling performance.

How to Interpret:

  1. Axes
    • X-axis (Fragment Counts): Total fragments per cell (log scale).
    • Y-axis (TSS Enrichment): TSS enrichment score per cell.
  2. Quality assessment
    • Top-right: High fragment count + high TSS enrichment, usually high-quality real cells.
    • Bottom-left: Low fragment count + low TSS enrichment, usually background/noise and filtered out.
    • Ideally, high-quality cells and background should be clearly separable.

docs.title: Saturation Curve
docs.text:
Chart Function: Evaluates sequencing depth sufficiency and library complexity, that is, whether additional sequencing can still identify substantial numbers of new unique fragments.

How to Interpret:

  1. Axes
    • X-axis: Mean read pairs per cell (sequencing depth).
    • Y-axis: Median unique fragments per cell.
  2. Curve behavior
    • Linear/rising phase: Additional sequencing yields many new unique fragments.
    • Plateau/saturation phase: Library complexity is mostly exhausted; additional sequencing gives diminishing returns.
  3. Quality guidance
    • A saturation (duplication-related) level around 20%-50% is often a practical balance between cost and completeness.

docs.title: Bead Similarity Ranking
docs.text:
Chart Function: In C4 ATAC, this plot is used to merge multiple beads from the same droplet by ranking bead pairs using Jaccard similarity.

How to Interpret:

  1. Axes
    • X-axis: All bead pairs ranked by Jaccard similarity (descending).
    • Y-axis: Jaccard similarity index (log scale).
  2. Key regions
    • Blue region: Similarity above the Otsu-derived threshold; bead pairs are considered from the same cell and merged.
    • Gray region: Similarity below threshold; bead pairs are treated as from different cells.

docs.title: scRNA Analysis Output
docs.text: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Output File Guide

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
After the single-cell RNA analysis is complete, a standardized file and subdirectory structure is generated in the specified output directory for gene expression profile analysis and cell type identification. This document describes the content, format, and intended use of each output file.

Tip: All output files use standard formats compatible with mainstream single-cell analysis tools (such as Scanpy, Seurat, etc.) and follow internationally recognized data format specifications.

docs.title: Output Directory Structure
docs.text:
outs/
├── analysis/
│   ├── cluster.csv
│   ├── cell_classification.csv             # mixed-species only
│   ├── marker.csv
│   └── QC_Cluster.h5ad
├── anno_decon_sorted.bam                   # when BAM enabled
├── anno_decon_sorted.bam.bai                # or .csi
├── oligo.records.bam                       # when BAM enabled
├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad
├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5
├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix/
│   ├── barcodes.tsv.gz
│   ├── features.tsv.gz
│   └── matrix.mtx.gz
├── raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5
├── raw_feature_bc_matrix/
│   ├── barcodes.tsv.gz
│   ├── features.tsv.gz
│   └── matrix.mtx.gz
├── metrics_summary.xls
├── singlecell.csv
└── <sample>_scRNA_report.html

filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad holds filtered counts; analysis/QC_Cluster.h5ad holds the clustered object. BAM indexes can be BAI or CSI. --no_bam skips cDNA and oligo BAMs. For multiplexed output, see C6 outputs.

docs.title: Alignment and Annotation Files
docs.text: Core Content: Result files from aligning raw sequencing data to the reference genome, containing complete alignment information and cell barcode tags.

docs.title: anno_decon_sorted.bam
docs.text:
This is the scRNA-seq alignment result file containing all raw data.

  • Core Purpose:

    • In-depth Analysis and Visualization: Can be used for deep visualization in genome browsers like IGV to inspect alignment situations and splicing patterns at specific gene loci.
    • Custom Analysis: Provides raw input for users who need to directly manipulate alignment-level data, such as for alternative splicing analysis, RNA velocity analysis, etc.

  • Content and Format:

    • Uses the international standard BAM (Binary Alignment Map) format.
    • The file is sorted by genomic coordinates and indexed (the .bai file), allowing for fast random access.
    • Each read is tagged with cell origin, UMI, and gene annotation information through TAG fields.

  • Key TAG Field Descriptions:

    • The BAM file uses rich TAG fields to store single-cell specific information, mainly divided into cell/molecule identifiers and gene annotations.

    Cell and Molecular Identifier Tags:

    Tag Type Description Biological Significance CB String Cell ID after merging cell barcodes Used to assign reads to a specific cell; it is the final cell ID after error correction and merging. CC String Error-corrected cell barcode sequence The corrected cell barcode, an intermediate step in generating the CB tag. CR String Raw sequencing cell barcode Retains original sequencing information for quality assessment and error tracing. CY String Cell barcode quality score Phred quality score, assessing the reliability of barcode sequencing. UB String Error-corrected UMI sequence Used for molecular deduplication to identify PCR duplicates and original mRNA molecules. UR String Raw sequencing UMI sequence Retains original UMI information for quality assessment and algorithm optimization. UY String UMI quality score Phred quality score, assessing the accuracy of UMI sequencing.

    Gene Annotation and Functional Tags:

    Tag Type Description Functional Purpose GX String Ensembl ID The primary ID for gene expression quantification. GN String Gene name Facilitates biological interpretation and supports gene function annotation. TX String Transcript ID Used for transcript-level expression analysis and alternative splicing studies. AN String Antisense transcript tag Identifies antisense RNA, assessing library directionality and non-coding RNA expression. RE String Genomic region type Distinguishes between Exon (E), Intron (N), and Intergenic (I) regions for transcriptome feature analysis.

docs.title: anno_decon_sorted.bam.bai
docs.text:
The index file for anno_decon_sorted.bam.

  • Core Purpose:
    • Fast Data Access: Allows tools like IGV and Samtools to quickly jump to and read alignment data for any genomic region without loading the entire BAM file.
    • Performance Guarantee: Ensures performance for all random access operations on the BAM file.
  • Format and Description:

    • The index file is generated by the samtools index command. To accommodate genomes of different sizes, the pipeline automatically selects the appropriate index format (BAI or CSI).

      Format Type Usage Instructions BAI Format The default index format, offering the best compatibility and suitable for most analysis tools and genomes. CSI Format Automatically generated when the BAM file contains chromosomes longer than 512 Mbp (2^29-1 bp) to support very large genomes.

docs.title: Feature Matrix Files
docs.text: Core Content: Single-cell gene expression count matrices, divided into raw and quality-controlled filtered data, using standard sparse matrix or AnnData format.

docs.title: Filtered Gene Expression Matrix (filtered_feature_bc_matrix/)
docs.text:
Contains the gene expression count matrix after filtering for high-quality cells, which is the core data for downstream quantitative analysis.

  • Core Purpose:

    • Downstream Quantitative Analysis: Serves as the primary input for analyses such as cell clustering and differential expression analysis.
    • High-Quality Data: Includes only barcodes identified as real cells, ensuring the accuracy of the analysis results.

  • Content and Format:

    • Uses the standard Matrix Market Exchange (MEX) format (for more on matrix formats, see Matrix Market Format Description), consisting of the following three compressed files: File Name Content Description barcodes.tsv.gz A list of cell IDs, identifying high-quality cells that passed QC. Each line contains one cell ID, corresponding to the column index of the matrix. features.tsv.gz A gene/feature information file, containing gene ID, name, and type. Each line contains three columns of information, corresponding to the row index of the matrix. matrix.mtx.gz The gene expression count matrix in Matrix Market format. Contains matrix dimension information and the row, column indices, and values of non-zero elements.

  • Format Advantages:

    • Space Efficient: The sparse matrix format (.mtx) only stores non-zero elements, greatly saving storage space.
    • Highly Compatible: The MEX format is a standard in the single-cell community, compatible with almost all mainstream analysis tools like Seurat and Scanpy.

docs.title: Raw Gene Expression Matrix (raw_feature_bc_matrix/)
docs.text:
Contains the raw gene expression count matrix for all detected cell barcodes (unfiltered).

  • Core Purpose:

    • Quality Control Assessment: Can be used to evaluate the effectiveness of cell filtering or to perform manual filtering based on custom criteria.
    • Data Integrity: Retains all original data, which can be used for deep mining or re-analysis if needed.

  • Content and Format:

    • Uses the standard Matrix Market Exchange (MEX) format, with a file composition identical to the filtered_feature_bc_matrix/ directory.
    • Includes all detected barcodes, including high-quality cells, low-quality cells, and background droplets.

docs.title: filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad
docs.text:
The feature matrix after cell identification and filtering, stored in AnnData (.h5ad) format. It is an alternative and supplement to the contents of the filtered_feature_bc_matrix/ directory.

  • Core Purpose:
    • Python Ecosystem Integration: Serves as the standard input format for Python single-cell analysis libraries like scanpy, seamlessly connecting to downstream analysis.
    • Data Integration: A single file can encapsulate the expression matrix, cell metadata, and gene metadata, making it easy to manage and share.
  • Content and Format:
    • A binary format based on HDF5. For details, refer to the AnnData Format Description.

docs.title: Analysis Results Directory (analysis/)
docs.text: Core Content: Results of downstream bioinformatics analysis, including cell clustering, differential genes, and post-QC data.

docs.title: cluster.csv
docs.text:
The cell clustering analysis result file in CSV format. It contains each cell's ID, its assigned cluster, dimensionality reduction coordinates, and key QC metrics.

  • Core Purpose:
    • Clustering Result Visualization: Can be directly used in plotting software to visualize UMAP dimensionality reduction results.
    • Basis for Cell Annotation: Provides basic grouping information for manual or automatic cell type annotation.
  • Content and Format:
    • Each row represents a high-quality cell, with major columns including:
      • Barcode: Cell ID
      • Cluster: The cluster number the cell belongs to
      • UMAP_1, UMAP_2: The 2D coordinates from UMAP dimensionality reduction
      • nGene, nUMI: The number of genes and UMIs detected in each cell

docs.title: cell_classification.csv (Dual-species analysis only)
docs.text:
A cell-level species assignment file generated for dual-species analyses (e.g., hg38 + mm10), in CSV format.

  • Core Purpose:
    • Species assignment per cell: Determines which species each cell primarily originates from.
    • Mixed-cell detection: Flags potential doublets/mixed cells (Multiplet) for downstream filtering or separate analysis.
  • Content and Format:
    • Each row represents one cell barcode, with major columns including:
      • barcode: Cell barcode ID
      • hg38: Count assigned to human reference (hg38)
      • mm10: Count assigned to mouse reference (mm10)
      • call: Species assignment result (hg38 / mm10 / Multiplet)

Example:
